hypotheses.claim: At least one of four pre-declared signals (mom_h, vwap_dev, or_pos, rvol_ratio) measured on NIFTY 1-minute index bars carries directional information about the forward h-minute index return at h in {5,15,30,60}, strongly enough to matter economically at Amendment E's capital. Specifically: some (signal, horizon) cell shows a Spearman IC whose |t| clears the Section 4 noise bar for N=16 (|t| >= 2.36), with the SAME IC sign in each of the four calendar years measured separately (2022 partial, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 partial — Amendment D5's sign-consistency rule applied to time rather than liquidity era), AND whose implied gross edge per trade at that horizon is at least 2x the net per-trade target from Amendment E5. Direction is NOT predicted: both momentum (IC>0) and reversal (IC<0) count, which is why the bar is two-sided and the sign-consistency requirement is what stops a sign flip across years being read as a finding.
hypotheses.kill_criterion: KILLED if no (signal, horizon) cell satisfies all three conditions together: (a) |t| >= 2.36 on the pooled Spearman IC, (b) the same IC sign in every calendar year with at least 60 trading days of data, and (c) implied gross edge per trade >= 2x the Amendment E5 net target at that horizon's achievable trade frequency. A cell that clears (a) but fails (b) is a sign-unstable estimate and is NOT a finding — that is the D5 lesson. A cell that clears (a) and (b) but fails (c) is real but too small to trade at this capital, and is recorded as such rather than carried forward. This screen can only kill or advance; per Amendment B5 it cannot promote anything.

signals.mom_h: return over the trailing h minutes (momentum if IC>0, reversal if IC<0)
signals.vwap_dev: (price - session VWAP) / trailing 30-min stdev of price
signals.or_pos: position in the first-15-min opening range: (p - OR_low)/(OR_high - OR_low)
signals.rvol_ratio: trailing 30-min realised vol / that session's median 30-min realised vol

hypotheses.note: Arena 5, screen 1, and the RESUME.md Step-4 'measure before building' item. Runs on data/intraday/NIFTY/index.parquet (370,626 1-min bars, 992 trading days, 2022-08-16..2026-08-14), archived from Dhan on 2026-08-14. gate='strict' is recorded for form only: this screen computes correlations on index bars and executes no fills, so no liquidity gate applies to it. Any STRATEGY descending from a surviving cell must be re-run under a real gate. equity is registered at the BOTTOM of Amendment E's Rs 50k-1L range, which is the conservative choice for the economic condition (c). Killing this hypothesis does not by itself close arena 'intraday_index' — Section 7 leaves arena closure an operator decision recorded with its grounds, and Section 8 fixes no screen allotment. It would, however, close the specific idea that a single unconditional signal predicts intraday index direction.

detail.why_killed: Conditions (a) and (b) both PASSED for 8 of 16 cells: the ICs are statistically significant after correcting for the overlap of forward windows, and sign-stable in all five calendar years. The kill is entirely on (c). The best cells (vwap_dev and or_pos at h=60, IC ~0.053) imply a 3.0-index-point expected move, worth Rs ~97 gross on one lot at delta 0.5 — against Rs 147 of round-trip cost at the project's registered 0.75/leg spread. Breakeven needs a spread under ~Rs 0.36/leg, about 1.9% of a Rs 19 option, which is tighter than NIFTY's cheap-option book actually quotes. At ZERO spread the same cells net only Rs ~48, and every cell at h<=30 loses money even then.
detail.measured_absence_not_absent_evidence: This is a measured absence, like Arena 1 and Arena 4, not an absence of evidence. The predictability is REAL and stable across four years; it is simply smaller than the bid-ask spread. Nothing here suggests looking harder at the same signals would help — a larger sample would only measure the same too-small effect more precisely.
detail.biases_favour_the_dead_hypothesis: Every approximation in the translation biases the estimate UPWARD, so the true edge is smaller than the number that failed: (i) it assumes a full position on every signal, ignoring the E[|z|]~0.8 factor for signal strength; (ii) it holds delta constant at 0.5 and charges no theta over the 60-minute hold; (iii) it charges no market impact. The kill is therefore conservative.
detail.artifact_found_and_removed: A fourth signal, rvol_ratio, initially produced the strongest result in the screen (IC 0.084, t 5.75, sign-consistent across all years). It was pure lookahead: its normaliser was the session median of realised vol, computed over the WHOLE session, so the 10:00 value knew 15:00. With an expanding (past-only) median it fails condition (a) at every horizon and disappears from the screen entirely. Recorded because it is exactly the kind of result that would have been reported as a discovery.
detail.not_tested_here: This screen tests UNCONDITIONAL single signals. It does not test conditional or interaction effects, nor does it test whether a larger per-trade edge exists at horizons beyond 60 minutes. Those would be separate registrations against a fresh comparisons budget.

detail.what: Measured the real NIFTY option bid-ask, the constant screen 1's kill rested on.
detail.sample: 312 contracts, 260 traded, 2 expiries (4 and 11 DTE), ONE after-hours snapshot of the 15:39 closing book on 2026-08-14
detail.verdict: KILL STANDS — and on measured cost, not assumed cost.
detail.the_correction_runs_against_the_hypothes: The raw spread is indeed tighter than assumed: median Rs 0.25/leg against a Rs 0.75 default. But converting to index points reverses the conclusion. Screen 1 paired a Rs 19 premium with an ATM delta of 0.5, and those are inconsistent — a Rs 19 NIFTY option has delta ~0.09. That inconsistency made the ORIGINAL economics too GENEROUS, not too harsh: it implied 3.0 index points of round-trip cost where the true figure at that premium is 12.87.
detail.irreducible_floor: With PERFECT limit fills and zero slippage, statutory charges alone cost 2.20 index points round trip at the ATM bucket, against a 2.995-point edge. The floor cannot be executed away — it is the exchange's and the government's cut — and it consumes 73% of the entire measured edge before any spread is paid.
detail.spread_is_not_the_dominant_cost: At the ATM bucket the spread is Rs 50.38 and statutory charges are Rs 61.44. Statutory is the LARGER half. This matters because execution skill can attack the spread and cannot touch the other.
detail.the_structural_squeeze: Cost per index point is minimised at ATM and rises steeply as premium falls, because a low-delta option buys very little index exposure per lot while the near-flat statutory charge per lot does not fall with it. But ATM is exactly what this capital cannot hold: one ATM lot is Rs 7,609, and a -40% stop on it is 6.1% of a Rs 50,000 account against a 1-2% per-trade budget. The contract whose cost structure works is unaffordable, and the contract that is affordable costs 12.87 points against a 2.995-point edge. At Rs 50k-1L there is NO contract on the board where this edge exceeds its round-trip cost — the best case anywhere, ignoring risk limits entirely, is still 4.01 vs 2.995.
detail.caveats: ONE after-hours snapshot of the closing book, 2 expiries, 10-12 contracts per mid-premium bucket. Intraday spreads may differ and must be sampled during a session before this is treated as a distribution. Note however that the statutory floor is independent of the spread and of sampling time, and the floor alone already takes 73% of the edge.

hypotheses.claim: An IN-SAMPLE optimal linear combination of a rich intraday feature set (20+ features: multi-lag momentum, VWAP deviation, opening-range position, realised-vol state, range position, acceleration, time-of-day) achieves, at its best horizon and best signal-strength threshold, a per-trade edge in INDEX POINTS exceeding the cheapest measured round-trip cost at that horizon. Costs are the measured ones from Amendment E9: NIFTY options 4.01 points transaction plus theta of 5.45 pts/hr at 4 DTE, or NIFTY futures 7.71 points with no theta; the cheaper of the two is used at each horizon, which favours the claim. Because the fit is in-sample and overfitted with no hold-out, and because horizon and threshold are chosen after seeing every result, the edge produced is an UPPER BOUND on what any out-of-sample strategy in this arena could achieve.
hypotheses.kill_criterion: KILLED, and arena 'intraday_index' recommended for closure, if the in-sample overfitted upper-bound edge fails to exceed the cheapest measured cost floor at EVERY horizon in {15,30,60,120,240,375} minutes and at every conditioning threshold tested. The logic is one-directional and deliberate: no out-of-sample strategy can beat an in-sample fit on the same features, so a bound that fails the economics closes the space rather than merely this attempt. IF THE BOUND CLEARS, THAT IS NOT A FINDING and must not be reported as one — an overfit in-sample fit clearing a bar is expected, carries no out-of-sample content, and leaves the arena exactly as open as it was. In that case the hypothesis is recorded as 'not closed' rather than 'survived', and the next step would be an honest walk-forward of the specific combination, registered separately.

hypotheses.note: Arena 5, ceiling screen, prompted by screen 1's kill (intraday-ic-modern) and by the cost measurement in Amendment E9. Runs on data/intraday/NIFTY/index.parquet (370,626 1-min bars, 992 trading days, 2022-08-16..2026-08-14). gate='strict' recorded for form: this computes correlations and a linear fit on index bars and executes no fills. Every feature must be past-only — rolling or expanding, never a session-wide aggregate. Screen 1 was nearly derailed by an rvol_ratio normalised on the whole session median, which made it the strongest signal in the screen until the lookahead was found. equity registered at the bottom of Amendment E's Rs 50k-1L range.

detail.verdict: NOT CLOSED — and per the registered kill criterion this is NOT a finding.
detail.what_the_registration_said_about_this_ou: The kill criterion, written before the run, said: 'IF THE BOUND CLEARS, THAT IS NOT A FINDING and must not be reported as one — an overfit in-sample fit clearing a bar is expected, carries no out-of-sample content, and leaves the arena exactly as open as it was.' It cleared. It is recorded as not_closed, not as survived. The arena stays open; nothing has been demonstrated.
detail.the_actually_informative_result: Screen 1's best SINGLE hand-picked feature, with no fitting whatsoever, reached IC 0.0537 at h=60. This screen's TWENTY-SIX features, combined by an OLS fit with no hold-out on 133,473 rows — i.e. free to overfit as much as it likes — reached IC 0.0539. The incremental IC bought by 25 extra features plus unrestricted overfitting is +0.0002. As far as this family of features can see, the information in intraday NIFTY index bars is already fully captured by one simple signal. That is a ceiling result even though it did not trip the economic kill.
detail.where_the_positive_cells_live: At threshold 0 — every bar, no selection — EVERY horizon is net negative, which agrees with screen 1. Positive cells appear only under aggressive conditioning, on 1.4%-21.6% of bars. That is precisely where an OLS fit's overfitting concentrates: a fitted model's most extreme predictions are its least reliable, and selecting on |z| of the fitted value selects the fit's own noise.
detail.long_horizons_are_untestable_intraday: h=240 and h=375 returned zero usable rows. A forward return of that length must complete inside the same session, and a 375-bar session leaves almost nothing. Multi-hour holds therefore require carrying overnight, which is a different strategy class with different risk and different costs — not a longer version of this one.
detail.what_this_licenses: Exactly one thing, named in the registration: an honest out-of-sample test of a SPECIFIC combination, registered separately. The cleanest such test is the conditional version of screen 1's unfitted signals — conditioning was explicitly outside screen 1's scope, and a single unfitted signal cannot overfit, so a threshold is the only free parameter.

detail.why_this_is_not_a_re_reading_of_its_own_: Stated plainly because it matters for auditability: this hypothesis's OWN kill criterion was NOT met. It said 'KILLED if the in-sample bound fails to exceed the cost floor at EVERY horizon and threshold'. The bound cleared at 13 of 20 cells, so that route to a kill was never available, and it is not being invoked now. Its claim — that an overfitted in-sample fit can clear the floor — was simply TRUE, and the registration said in advance that this would carry no information.
detail.what_actually_resolves_it: The registration named its own successor: 'the ONLY thing this licenses is an honest walk-forward of a specific combination, registered separately', and identified the cleanest such test as the conditional version of screen 1's unfitted signals. That test was registered as intraday-conditional-modern and was KILLED — 0 of 14 cells significantly positive, 0 of 14 beating a 7% FD, and most significantly negative after costs. Since nothing was fitted there, the in-sample bound measured here is confirmed as an overfitting artifact rather than a signal that honest testing might have recovered.
detail.terminal_status_reasoning: Marked 'killed' rather than left at 'not_closed'. 'survived' would be actively dangerous — in this registry it means 'candidate for paper trading', which this is emphatically not. Leaving it 'not_closed' forever would block arena closure over a question that has in fact been answered. 'killed' with this event attached is the honest and auditable option: the question it opened is closed, and closed against it.
detail.what_it_contributed: The durable result is not the verdict but the measurement: 26 features combined by an OLS fit with no hold-out on 133,473 rows reached IC 0.0539 at h=60, against 0.0537 for ONE hand-picked unfitted signal. An incremental +0.0002 for 25 extra features plus unrestricted overfitting. As far as this feature family can see, the information in intraday NIFTY index bars is exhausted by a single simple signal.

hypotheses.claim: Taking only the strongest readings of screen 1's two surviving unfitted signals (vwap_dev and or_pos) produces a per-trade edge that clears the measured cost floor. Specifically: for some (signal, horizon in {60,120}, threshold in {1.0,1.5,2.0,2.5}) cell, going LONG when the past-only standardised signal z >= +threshold and SHORT when z <= -threshold — MOMENTUM, the direction screen 1 measured — yields a mean net edge per trade, after the Amendment E9 cost of the cheapest instrument at that horizon, that is positive in every calendar year, significant against the Section 4 bar for N=16, frequent enough to be validated, and large enough to beat a 7% fixed deposit on the capital required to run it. Nothing is fitted: the signals are screen 1's fixed formulas, the standardisation is expanding and past-only, and the threshold is the sole free parameter.
hypotheses.kill_criterion: KILLED unless at least one cell satisfies ALL FOUR: (a) mean net edge per trade > 0 in EVERY calendar year holding >= 60 trading days — Amendment D5's sign-consistency rule applied to the NET figure, not the IC, so a signal that only works in one regime cannot pass; (b) pooled net edge > 0 with |t| >= 2.35, the Section 4 bar at N=16; (c) >= 30 trades per year, so Section 3's detectability rule is satisfiable inside the 2027-01-07 stop date; (d) implied annual net return > 7% of the capital required to run it — Section 1's benchmark — counting Rs 7,609 per ATM option lot or ~Rs 1,90,000 of futures margin as appropriate to the instrument the cost was taken from. A cell clearing (a)-(c) but failing (d) is real but not worth doing, and is recorded as such rather than carried forward. If NOTHING clears, arena 'intraday_index' is recommended for closure: screen 1 killed the unconditional case, the ceiling screen showed the feature space is exhausted, and this closes the conditional case. Per Amendment B5 this screen cannot promote — clearing means 'worth a walk-forward', never 'works'.

signals.vwap_dev: (price - expanding session VWAP) / rolling 30-bar sd of price

config.direction: MOMENTUM — long when z >= +thr, short when z <= -thr
config.fitting: NONE — no coefficients, no weights, no feature selection

hypotheses.note: Arena 5, screen 3 and the last cheap question in it. Prompted by intraday-ic-modern (unconditional, killed on economics: 2.995 index points against a 4.01-7.71 point floor) and intraday-ceiling-modern (not closed, but showed 26 overfitted features add +0.0002 IC over one signal). Runs on data/intraday/NIFTY/index.parquet, 370,626 1-min bars, 992 trading days. Costs are the MEASURED ones from Amendment E9 rather than the engine default: options 4.01 points transaction + 5.45 pts/hr theta at 4 DTE, futures 7.71 points all-in with no theta; the cheaper at each horizon is used, which favours the claim. gate='strict' recorded for form; this executes no fills. Standardisation MUST be expanding/past-only — screen 1 was nearly derailed by a whole-session median normaliser, and the same trap applies to the z used here. Only bars whose forward window closes inside the same session are counted; no overnight carry, which is a different strategy class.

detail.verdict: KILLED — 0 of 14 cells significantly positive, 0 of 14 beat a 7% FD.
detail.direction_was_declared_in_advance: MOMENTUM was registered before the run, from screen 1's positive ICs. The measured result is not merely insignificant but mostly significantly NEGATIVE after costs (t = -5.21, -3.71, -3.25 on the highest-frequency cells). Conditioned momentum actively loses. Because the sign was declared first, this cannot be re-read as the discovery of a reversal effect.
detail.conditioning_underdelivers_versus_linear: The case for running this screen rested on a normal-theory extrapolation: E[|z| given |z|>k] implies the edge should scale to 4.57 pts at k=1.0, 5.81 at 1.5, 7.12 at 2.0, 8.47 at 2.5. MEASURED at h=60: 2.35, 2.88, 2.24, 5.39 — short by 2.2 to 4.9 points at every threshold, and not even monotonic in k. The signal-return relation is not linear in z and the tails deliver less than proportionally, so that extrapolation was too optimistic and is recorded here as superseded by measurement.
detail.the_gap_that_kills_it: Cost floor 7.71 index points (futures, the cheapest instrument at these horizons). Best measured GROSS edge at h=60 across all thresholds: 5.39. The edge does not reach the cost before any of the statistical tests are applied.
detail.no_overfitting_available_as_an_excuse: Nothing was fitted: screen 1's fixed formulas, expanding past-only standardisation, threshold the sole free parameter. So this result cannot be attributed to a bad fit, and it cannot be rescued by a better one.
detail.bug_found_and_fixed_before_recording: The first run counted every qualifying BAR as a trade, ignoring that a 60-minute hold overlaps the next 59 bars. It reported 19,354 trades/yr (77 a day, when ~6 non-overlapping positions fit a 375-bar session) and annual returns of -2853% to +782%. Rerun with non-overlapping trades the counts are 56-720/yr and returns -132% to +6.9%. The kill was unchanged either way — it rests on condition (b), whose t-stat already corrected for overlap — but the broken figures were not allowed into this record.
detail.arena_recommendation: Arena 'intraday_index' RECOMMENDED FOR CLOSURE. The three screens together cover the space: intraday-ic-modern killed the unconditional case on economics; intraday-ceiling-modern showed 26 overfitted features add +0.0002 IC over one signal, so the feature space is exhausted; this screen kills the conditional case on both significance and economics. Section 7 leaves closure to the operator, so it is recorded as a recommendation, not executed.

hypotheses.claim: Some combination of horizon (60 or 120 min), past-only trailing-volatility regime (low/mid/high tercile) and signal-strength threshold (|z| >= 1.0, 1.5, 2.0) yields an OUT-OF-SAMPLE gross edge of at least 8.0 index points per non-overlapping round trip, using a multivariate model trained only on data preceding each test year. 8.0 points is Arena 5's registered reopening threshold: it is the level at which a gross edge clears the measured 7.71-point all-in cost floor with margin to spare. The mechanism under test is REGIME conditioning, not signal improvement — the same predictive skill applied where the forward distribution is widest should scale the edge in points even at unchanged IC, because edge = IC x sd and sd varies several-fold across volatility regimes.
hypotheses.kill_criterion: KILLED unless at least one (horizon, vol regime, threshold) cell satisfies ALL of: (a) mean OUT-OF-SAMPLE gross edge >= 8.0 index points per non-overlapping trade, pooled across test years 2023-2026; (b) mean NET edge > 0 after the measured Amendment E9 cost floor for the cheapest instrument at that horizon; (c) net edge > 0 in EVERY test year, not merely pooled — D5's sign-consistency applied out-of-sample; (d) pooled |t| >= 2.41, the Section 4 bar at N=18; (e) >= 30 trades per year, so Section 3's detectability is satisfiable. If NOTHING clears, the answer to 'does any intraday edge reach 8 points' is NO for this feature family under regime conditioning, Arena 5's reopening condition #2 is demonstrably unmet, and arena 'intraday_session' is recommended for closure alongside it. Per Amendment B5 clearing means 'worth a walk-forward at strategy level', never 'works'.

config.method: walk-forward by calendar year; train on all prior, test on year
config.vol_regimes: terciles of trailing 30-bar realised vol, cut on TRAIN only
config.mechanism: regime conditioning (edge = IC x sd; sd varies by regime)

hypotheses.note: Prompted by the operator's question after arena intraday_index was closed on 2026-08-14. Tests that arena's own reopening condition #2 (a gross edge >= 8 index points from a genuinely different family) via the one lever its three screens did NOT test: conditioning on the volatility REGIME rather than on the signal. Registered in intraday_session because that is the open arena whose definition covers session and regime structure; it is not a backdoor registration into the closed arena, and if it clears, reopening intraday_index would still require the charter amendment its closure record demands. Runs on data/intraday/NIFTY/index.parquet (370,626 1-min bars, 992 days). Walk-forward by calendar year: train on all prior data, test on the year. Costs are the measured Amendment E9 figures (options 4.01 + 5.45/hr theta at 4 DTE; futures 7.71 all-in), cheaper instrument per horizon. All conditioning variables must be past-only; volatility terciles are cut on TRAILING realised vol using thresholds fixed from the training period only, never from the test year. Only forward windows closing inside the same session count.

detail.verdict: KILLED — 0 of 18 on every condition except trade count.
detail.answer_to_the_question: NO. No intraday edge reaches 8 index points out of sample. The best cell anywhere is 7.70 gross (h=60, high-vol regime, |z|>=2.0) against a 7.71-point cost floor — a net of -0.01 points, dead on breakeven before any execution error, and short of the 8.0 bar.
detail.and_the_best_cell_is_not_even_that: Its per-year record is 2024 gross -5.2, 2025 +14.7, 2026 +43.9. The pooled 7.70 is carried entirely by 41 trades in 2026. That is Section 6.7's 'single good configuration surrounded by bad ones' and fails Amendment D5's sign-consistency outright — 2 of 3 years positive, not 3 of 3. The honest reading is that the top of the table is one lucky year, so the true best is lower than 7.70, not merely short of 8.
detail.the_regime_lever_worked_directionally_an: Worth recording because the mechanism was correctly predicted and still did not save it. Mean OOS gross by volatility regime: low -0.83, mid -2.56, HIGH +2.21 pts, with the best cell in every horizon coming from the high-vol stratum. So edge = IC x sd does scale the edge in points where the distribution is widest, exactly as registered. It simply does not scale far enough: applying the same skill where moves are larger scales the noise with them.
detail.the_fit_has_no_out_of_sample_skill: 11 of 18 cells have NEGATIVE out-of-sample gross edge — before costs. A walk-forward multivariate model trained on all prior years is worse than the single unfitted signal of screen 1, which at least had a positive IC. This is consistent with intraday-ceiling-modern's +0.0002: with nothing left to learn, the fit learns noise, so fitting actively HURTS out of sample.
detail.what_this_closes: Arena intraday_index's reopening condition #2 — 'a gross edge >= 8 index points from a genuinely different signal family' — is demonstrably UNMET, tested out-of-sample via the one lever its own screens never used. Condition #2 should not be re-attempted with another signal set; the ceiling screen already showed the feature family is exhausted and this shows the regime lever does not close the gap either. Conditions #1 (a cost floor below ~3.0 points) and #3 (a different holding regime, which would be a new arena) remain the only live routes back.
detail.arena_recommendation: Arena 'intraday_session' RECOMMENDED FOR CLOSURE, per this hypothesis's own registered kill criterion. Session and regime structure were the lever under test and they do not produce a tradeable edge. Note this does NOT automatically close 'intraday_option': everything here is DIRECTIONAL, and non-directional option structures were not tested by it — though Arena 1 already killed short volatility on size-independent grounds, and the same measured cost floor applies to anything crossing the same book.

futures_trend.grounds: Closed on resolvability and throughput, NOT on demonstrated absence of edge. T2 established the arena is not structurally capped: the perfect-foresight oracle reaches Sharpe 8.9, friction is irrelevant, and N_eff 2.59 does not prevent an 8-name book reaching 1.0 — IC ~0.05 would suffice. What closes it is that the question cannot be answered with the data available. On modern the smallest detectable IC (0.0551) exceeds the IC required to be tradeable (~0.04-0.05), and pooling more history is inadmissible under Amendment D5, which admits 0 of 11 estimates because signal properties are not stable across eras even where instrument properties are. Eleven candidate signals were measured and the largest was |t| 1.56 against a 2.19 bar. Two hypotheses registered, two killed, both on signal rather than plumbing.
futures_trend.reopen_requires: Either (a) a dataset that lifts the smallest detectable IC materially below 0.04 within a SINGLE era — a longer modern era, higher-frequency observations, or a materially wider universe — or (b) a signal class whose IC is pre-registered and then measured above 0.05 on modern alone, without pooling. Section 7 allows no extensions, so either route is a charter amendment rather than a registration.

index_structures.grounds: No edge was demonstrated, and the question WAS resolvable — this is the strong form of closure, not the resolvability form used for futures_trend. Two structures spanning the family's gamma range (iron butterfly with ATM shorts, iron condor with delta-0.18 shorts a median 6.8 intervals out) were each entered unconditionally on weekly NIFTY across the full modern era, each supplied an A5-sized sample (179 and 198 trades, ~50/year against A5's 32.3), and each lost: expectancy -Rs 705 and -Rs 406/trade, t -1.95 and -1.44, both NEGATIVE BEFORE FRICTION (gross -84,720 and -41,858). The +2.38 vol point VRP measured here is real and is payment for the left tail, not a mispricing: strip the 10 worst of the condor's 198 weeks and the book is +Rs 55,851, which is the short-vol payoff working as designed and losing anyway. The arena's other routes are separately closed — vanilla credit spreads excluded by Section 8, the calendar killed as cal-cheapvol-modern with its term structure measured flat at -0.00020 variance units (t -0.14), the reverse calendar measured and not worth building, and ratios unsizeable without an undefined-risk sizing rule that does not exist.
index_structures.reopen_requires: A structure in this arena that is NOT short volatility -- the two kills cover the short-vol family from ATM to 0.18-delta shorts and say nothing about long-vol or dispersion structures. Concretely: evidence that a long-gamma or relative-value index-option structure clears Section 4's bar on a sample A5 can use, OR a demonstration that the -2.38 vol point premium inverts in some identifiable and tradeable regime (not a regime filter fitted to these same 377 trades, which Section 6.3 forbids). A different wing width, delta target or exit rule on the SAME short-vol structures is a retry, not a reopening, and Section 7 does not permit it.

event_vol.grounds: No edge was demonstrated, and the question WAS resolvable — the strong form, as for index_structures. EARNINGS HALF: the volatility premium was MEASURED, not merely searched for. Across 246 single-stock earnings events in the modern era the mid-price P&L of a short ATM straddle is -Rs 174/trade, indistinguishable from zero; the -Rs 3,857/trade realised loss is bid-ask, not mispricing. Because a buyer pays the same spread, both directions are negative at EVERY slippage level INCLUDING ZERO, where the long side collects the +174 mid premium and still loses to statutory friction alone (Rs 311/trade). That robustness matters: slippage_per_leg=0.75 is an assumption, not a measurement, and this conclusion does not rest on it. The result is also structure-independent — a cheaper two-legged structure has nothing to recover from a premium of approximately zero. Three hypotheses closed (evol-earnings-modern, evol-earnings-pre2024, evol-earnings-narrowwing), the last with 246 trades at t = -9.08 and a MONOTONE wing sweep in which more sample is uniformly more loss. Capacity, once the true constraint was identified (a self-imposed risk cap at 45% of refusals, not market illiquidity at 12%), was fixed and is not the reason for closure. MACRO HALF: unregistrable against A5 by arithmetic — roughly 40 events in one liquidity era cannot reach 100 OOS trades by any route, even with a perfect calendar, and the calendar cannot be sourced anyway (FOMC parses 8-for-11 years, RBI's archive is ASP.NET postback-driven with no stable URL).
event_vol.reopen_requires: An event-vol structure whose edge does NOT depend on the straddle premium that was measured at zero here — the -Rs 174/trade mid-price figure covers ATM straddles with wings on the 60 most-liquid F&O names at 2-days-before / 1-day-after timing, and says nothing about skew, term structure across the event, or single-leg directional announcement drift (which is arguably cross_sectional, not this arena). Concretely: a measurement showing a non-zero MID-PRICE premium on some event-vol structure, taken on data other than these same 246 events, since fitting a subset or a timing to them is Section 6.3. A different wing, universe, or entry timing on the same short straddle is a retry, which Section 7 does not permit. The macro half additionally requires a verifiable RBI/Budget source AND a route to 100+ OOS events that does not exist at ~40 events per era.

cross_sectional.grounds: No edge was demonstrated, and the SEARCH BUDGET is exhausted rather than the question being exhaustively answered — this is a weaker closure than index_structures or event_vol, and is stated as such. What was measured: T2b scored eleven candidate signals (momentum at four lookbacks, reversal at two, low-vol, 52-week high, acceleration, OI change, volume trend) and nothing cleared — largest |rank IC| 0.0359, and NEGATIVE; largest |t| 1.56 against a 2.19 eleven-signal bar. xsect-mom-modern registered 12-1 momentum and died at t +0.13, with its own signal measured at rank IC -0.0139. This arena's remaining open condition was explicitly that it NOT be searched further: one pre-registered signal, because detectable IC is 0.0249 for one candidate but 0.0463 when fishing across eleven, against a required 0.054 — so a twelfth search would itself close the arena by spending the detectability margin. That one signal was spent on cross-sectional carry (annualised futures basis), declared with its direction and thresholds in ARENAS.md X1 and COMMITTED BEFORE COMPUTATION. It is refuted: rank IC -0.0270, t -2.22, 41 rebalances, 95% CI [-0.0508, -0.0032] against a required +0.0540 — wrong sign, entire CI below zero, and detectable (|IC| 0.0270 > the 0.0249 this sample can distinguish). The pre-declaration barred re-reading a negative result as 'short high carry works'. Data limitation recorded: UndrlygPric is empty for stock futures before 2024, so carry is computable on 2024+ only; this cannot change the verdict, because a positive pre-2024 estimate would fail D5.1 sign consistency and D1 would return the decision to a negative modern.
cross_sectional.reopen_requires: More rebalances, or a signal class this arena has not seen. Two concrete routes. (1) POWER: the binding number is 41 rebalances at a 15-trading-day horizon. UndrlygPric becoming available pre-2024, or a calendar-spread estimator of the same curve slope validated against the 2024+ figures, would roughly triple the sample and move detectable IC below 0.02 — but note D5.1 blocks any pooled estimate whose per-era signs disagree, so this only helps if the added history agrees with modern. (2) A GENUINELY NEW SIGNAL CLASS: everything tested is a function of past returns, volume, open interest, or the futures curve. Fundamentals (value, quality, accruals), borrow/short-interest data proper rather than its basis proxy, analyst revisions, and index-inclusion flow are all untouched and none is derivable from bhavcopy — each needs a data source this project does not have. Acquiring one of those is the honest reopening condition. A further lookback, weighting or horizon on the signals already scored is a retry, which Section 7 does not permit, and would in any case spend the detectability margin the arena no longer has.

intraday_index.grounds:
MEASURED ABSENCE OF A TRADEABLE EDGE — not absence of evidence, and not 'unresolvable with the data available'. The distinction matters and the evidence supports the stronger claim.

Intraday NIFTY is demonstrably NOT a random walk. Screen 1 found ICs that are significant after correcting for the overlap of forward windows AND sign-stable in every calendar year 2022-2026 (vwap_dev and or_pos both reach IC ~0.053 at h=60). The predictability is real. It is simply smaller than the cost of trading it.

The cost floor was MEASURED, not assumed (Amendment E9, 312 contracts from the live depth book): 4.01 index points round trip on ATM options plus 5.45 pts/hr of theta at 4 DTE, or 7.71 points all-in on futures with no theta. Statutory charges are the larger half of that and cannot be executed away — with PERFECT limit fills and zero slippage the floor is still 2.20 points, 73% of the entire measured edge. The best measured edge, at any horizon and any conditioning threshold, is 5.39 points against a 7.71-point floor.

Three screens cover the space between them:
  intraday-ic-modern          unconditional case killed on economics: 2.995 pts
                              of edge against a 4.01-7.71 pt floor.
  intraday-ceiling-modern     the feature space is exhausted. 26 features fitted
                              in-sample with NO hold-out on 133,473 rows reached
                              IC 0.0539 at h=60; ONE unfitted hand-picked signal
                              reached 0.0537. Incremental value of 25 extra
                              features plus unrestricted overfitting: +0.0002.
  intraday-conditional-modern conditional case killed on BOTH significance and
                              economics: 0 of 14 cells significantly positive,
                              0 of 14 beating a 7% FD, most significantly
                              NEGATIVE after costs. Nothing was fitted, so it
                              cannot be blamed on a bad fit or rescued by a
                              better one. Conditioning also underdelivered
                              linear-IC theory by 2.2-4.9 points at every
                              threshold.

Searching harder is not indicated: the ceiling screen shows better features are not available in this family, and a larger sample would only measure the same too-small effect more precisely.
intraday_index.reopen_requires:
A charter amendment, justified by ONE of the following. Nothing less reopens this arena; Section 7 allows no extensions.

1. A MATERIAL FALL IN THE COST FLOOR. The kill is a cost result, so it is    reversible by costs. Concretely: a measured all-in round-trip cost below    ~3.0 index points for an instrument this account can actually hold. That    would require a change in Indian F&O taxation (STT is the larger half of    the floor and dominates it at ATM), or an instrument with materially better    exposure-per-rupee than a 65-unit NIFTY lot. Re-measure with    backtest/option_spread.py before claiming it.

2. AN EDGE OF A DIFFERENT ORDER, from a signal family genuinely unlike those    tested. The bar is a measured gross edge of >= 8 index points per round    trip, sign-stable across years. Note this is ~2.7x the best unconditional    edge found and ~1.5x the best conditional one, so 'a slightly better    momentum signal' does not qualify. The tested family is multi-lag momentum,    VWAP deviation, opening-range position, realised-vol state, range position,    acceleration and time-of-day.

3. A DIFFERENT HOLDING REGIME. Everything here required the forward window to    close inside the same session; h=240 and h=375 returned zero usable rows for    that reason. Overnight and multi-day holds are a different strategy class    with different risk, different costs and no theta relief for long options,    and were never tested. They would be a NEW arena, not a reopening of this    one.

intraday_session.grounds:
MEASURED ABSENCE OF A TRADEABLE EDGE from session and regime structure — with one sub-space explicitly NOT covered, named in the reopening conditions below rather than glossed over.

The arena was tested by intraday-edgesize-modern, a walk-forward screen asking the decisive question directly: does ANY intraday edge reach 8.0 index points out of sample? 8.0 is arena intraday_index's registered reopening threshold — the level at which a gross edge clears the measured 7.71-point all-in cost floor with margin. Answer: NO. 0 of 18 cells cleared any condition except trade count.

The best cell anywhere was 7.70 gross points (h=60, high-vol regime, |z|>=2.0) against a 7.71-point floor — net -0.01, breakeven before any execution error. And it is weaker than that figure suggests: its per-year record is 2024 gross -5.2, 2025 +14.7, 2026 +43.9, so the pooled 7.70 rests entirely on 41 trades in one year. That is Section 6.7's 'single good configuration surrounded by bad ones' and fails D5 sign-consistency at 2 of 3 years. The honest best is BELOW 7.70.

The registered mechanism worked directionally and still failed, which is the most informative part. Mean out-of-sample gross by volatility regime: low -0.83, mid -2.56, HIGH +2.21, with the best cell at every horizon drawn from the high-vol stratum. So edge = IC x sd does scale the edge in points where the forward distribution is widest, exactly as predicted. It does not scale far enough: applying the same skill where moves are larger scales the noise with them.

And 11 of 18 cells had NEGATIVE out-of-sample gross edge before costs. A walk-forward model trained on all prior years is worse than a single unfitted signal. With nothing left to learn — intraday-ceiling-modern measured the incremental value of 25 extra features at +0.0002 IC — the fit learns noise, so fitting actively hurts out of sample.
intraday_session.reopen_requires:
A charter amendment justified by ONE of the following. Section 7 allows no extensions otherwise.

1. SCHEDULED-EVENT CONDITIONING, WHICH WAS NOT TESTED. This is a real gap and is    recorded as one. intraday-edgesize-modern conditioned on trailing volatility    regime and time of day, but NOT on proximity to scheduled macro events. The    data exists and is unused for this purpose: data/events/ holds RBI board    meetings 2016-2025 and backtest/macro_events.py carries an FOMC calendar with    coverage enforcement. Event days concentrate large moves, so the edge = IC x    sd argument has a further lever there. Reopening on this ground requires a    measured OOS gross edge >= 8.0 index points, sign-consistent across at least    three separate years — the three-year bar exists specifically because the best    cell here was one good year wearing a pooled average.

2. A MATERIAL FALL IN THE COST FLOOR: a measured all-in round-trip cost below    ~3.0 index points for an instrument this account can hold. Statutory charges    are the larger half of the current floor and dominate at ATM, so this needs a    change in Indian F&O taxation or materially better lot economics — not a    different broker. Re-measure with backtest/option_spread.py before claiming    it.

3. INTRADAY DATA THIS SCREEN DID NOT HAVE — order flow, book depth through the    session, or trade-level prints. Everything tested used 1-minute OHLC of the    index. A genuinely different information source is a different question, not    a retry of this one.

What does NOT reopen it: another directional signal set on 1-minute index bars. The feature family is measured as exhausted and regime conditioning is measured as insufficient.
evidence: arena intraday_index closure record (source of the 8.0-point bar)
